articles.title: Kerala Sthree Sakthi SS-541 Lottery Result Today (October 13): First prize ₹1 crore, check prize... - Moneycontrol.com
articles.full_text:
The Kerala State Lotteries Department is scheduled to conduct the Sthree Sakthi SS-541 lottery draw on Tuesday, October 13, 2026, with a first prize of ₹1 crore. The draw is scheduled for 3 pm at Gorky Bhavan near Bakery Junction in Thiruvananthapuram. The official results are expected to be published after the draw, with participants advised to verify their ticket numbers against the department’s official results.
The weekly lottery offers several prize categories, including ₹30 lakh for the second prize and ₹5 lakh for the third prize. Lower-tier prizes range from ₹100 to ₹5,000, while the consolation prize is ₹5,000 for eligible tickets from other series that match the first-prize number, subject to the official prize rules.
Sthree Sakthi tickets cost ₹50 each, while a book of tickets costs ₹750, according to the supplied details. Participants should retain their tickets and check the official result notification before making any claim.
Kerala Lottery Sthree Sakthi SS-541 prize structure
The SS-541 draw includes nine main prize categories and a consolation prize. The first three prizes are awarded to individual winning tickets, while the lower categories cover specified ticket-number endings. The official result notification should be used to confirm winning numbers and applicable series.
The published prize structure lists the first prize as common to all series. Winners should check the complete official notification for the precise winning numbers, series and eligibility requirements. The agent names and agency numbers associated with the top three prizes may also be included in the official result details.
Sthree Sakthi SS-541 result: How to check and claim prize money
Participants can check the Sthree Sakthi SS-541 result through the Kerala State Lotteries Department’s official website and result notification. The draw is scheduled for 3 pm, and results are generally published after the numbers have been verified. Participants should avoid relying solely on unofficial posts or unverified messages.
Winners must submit their tickets within 30 days of the draw date, according to the supplied claim guidance. The process depends on the prize amount. Prizes of ₹1 lakh or less can be claimed through the relevant District Lottery Office, while prizes above ₹1 lakh must be submitted to the Director of State Lotteries, subject to the department’s current rules.
The stated claim procedure includes the following steps:
- Check the ticket number and series against the official result.
- Sign the reverse of the original winning ticket and keep it secure.
- Submit the ticket within 30 days of the draw.
- For prizes of up to ₹1 lakh, approach the relevant District Lottery Office. For higher amounts, follow the Directorate of State Lotteries’ submission procedure.
- Provide the required claim form, identity documents, photographs and a self-attested PAN card copy, along with any other documents specified by the department.
Additional documentation may be required in particular cases. The supplied guidance mentions a guardianship certificate for minors and a joint declaration on ₹50 stamp paper for joint winners. Applicants should confirm the latest document requirements with the relevant lottery office before submitting a claim.
Kerala State Lotteries: Tax rules and public welfare
Kerala has operated its state lottery programme since 1967. Its weekly lotteries include Sthree Sakthi, Dhanalekshmi, Samrudhi, Suvarna Keralam, Bhagyathara, Karunya Plus and Karunya. The state also conducts bumper draws during the year, including the Christmas New Year, Summer, Vishu, Monsoon, Thiruvonam and Pooja lotteries.
Lottery winnings are taxable under Indian income tax rules. The supplied tax guidance cites a 30% rate under Section 194B, with health and education cess potentially taking the effective rate to 31.2%, before any applicable surcharge. Tax deducted at source and the final amount payable depend on the applicable rules and the size and nature of the prize. Winners should confirm the current tax treatment with the relevant authorities or a qualified tax professional.
Lottery proceeds also contribute to state revenue and support public spending. Figures provided for the 2021-22 financial year put revenue generated by the lottery system at approximately ₹9,000 crore. The funds are reported to support areas such as health, education, infrastructure, housing assistance and medical support, while ticket sales also provide employment and commission-based income for agents and sellers.
Participants awaiting the Sthree Sakthi SS-541 result should check the official notification before claiming a prize. The winning ticket must be preserved carefully, and all claims should be submitted within the prescribed deadline.
